records.applicability: undici 6.29.0 is bundled inside the pinned scanner, npm 11.21.1, which is installed from dependency-audit/scanner with scripts disabled and run only as npm audit. Its only requirer in the bundle is node_modules/node-gyp/lib/download.js (node-gyp 12.4.0, header downloads for native builds); npm's registry requests go through npm-registry-fetch and make-fetch-happen. Measured 2026-10-24 on Node 24.22.1, the major CI uses, with a preload that records every module file resolved through Module._resolveFilename and module.registerHooks: the scanner's exact audit argv, cwd and scrubbed environment, against the application graph and against its own graph, resolved no file under node_modules/undici and returned complete reports. node-gyp's lib/download.js was not resolved; node-gyp/bin/node-gyp.js was, only through require.resolve for the node-gyp config default, which runs none of its code. Positive controls under the same probe (requiring node-gyp/lib/download.js, and requiring undici from the bundle) each recorded 95 undici files. A scanner that crashed would leave the audit incomplete, which fails closed.
records.reason: As of 2026-10-24 no npm release bundles a fixed undici: 11.21.1 (the latest 11.x) and 12.2.1 (the latest release, which supports Node 24) both bundle 6.29.0, and the fix is 6.29.1. A bundled dependency cannot be replaced by the lockfile or an override, so without a disposition the scanner graph is blocking and no candidate is certified. The accepted residual risk is that the scanner loads undici on a path the measured runs did not take. Remove this record in the same change that moves the scanner to an npm that bundles undici 6.29.1 or later; it expires at 00:00 UTC on 2026-11-30, with Admin's matching record, and is not extended automatically.
